verdicts.question: What exactly did CPCB's January 2025 'Classification of Sectors into Red, Orange, Green, White and Blue Categories' change: how many sectors are in Annexure I (359 with 107/120/81/51 or 419 with 125/137/94/54/9), what pollution-index ranges define each colour, what the new Blue category means for consent validity, has KSPCB adopted the 2025 list in place of its 2016 Notification 1425 list, and what consent validity applies now to Red, Orange, Green and Blue units in Karnataka?
verdicts.problems: Verification limits first: the session's web-search budget is exhausted (200/200) and every outbound fetch is refused by the gateway, so none of the 16 cited sources could be re-confirmed by a fresh snippet today; checks below rest on repository evidence (the founder's notes taken from the attached CPCB report, an earlier run that opened cpcb.gov.in/categorization-of-industrial-sectors on 2026-07-20 and kspcb.karnataka.gov.in/consent-management/categorisation-rog on 2026-09-29, and sibling clusters). What holds: the 419 = 125/137/94/54/9 and 359 = 107/120/81/51 counts match the founder's own reading of the report (docs/plan/inputs/2026-09-30-founder-research-part-1/refined-roles-material-chains--4-cpcb-2025-cross-reference.csv, which says Annexure-I covers 359 industrial sectors) and the PI bands (Red >=80, Orange 55-80, Green 25-55, White <25) match the same note; arithmetic checks (107+120+81+51=359; 125+137+94+54+9=419; 419-359=60=9+51). But the '51 service/infrastructure sectors (18 Red, 17 Orange, 13 Green, 3 White)' is derived by subtraction, not read from any source, and the answer presents it as fact. Key claims not confirmed by snippet: (1) the Blue list of nine sectors and the +2-year CTO rule (HP PCB PDF, TeamLease 41310, Khaitan) - plausible, sources exist in earlier journals, but the exact nine items could not be checked, and the founder's note lists 'sewage/drainage networks' and 'E-waste collection' as Blue, so the disagreement is unresolved either way; (2) the Karnataka validity figures Red 5 / Orange 10 / Green 15 (TeamLease 5774, 'notification of 3 June 2019') and the micro-unit 'permanent Green consent' - no snippet content is visible in the repo for this, only the article title from a 30 Sep 2026 search, and the repo's own legal cluster (docs/plan/research/answers) states the opposite, 5/5/10 under Notification 1425 of 15 Jun 2016, citing the KSPCB categorisation page; the answer hard-codes 5/10/15 into the decision without resolving this conflict; (3) the attribution of circular KSPCB/258/2025-SEE-1 (28 March 2025) to KERALA is asserted without a snippet; Karnataka's board also uses the KSPCB prefix and has Senior Environmental Engineer (SEE) posts, so this circular may in fact be the Karnataka adoption the answer says it could not find - it must be read, not dismissed; (4) the 28 July 2025 amendment of G.S.R. 702(E)/703(E) (PI up to 25, Classification-2025 schedule) - TeamLease 45081 title only, content not confirmed; (5) '22 January 2025' publication date and 's.18(1)(b)' basis - not confirmed by any snippet in the repo (the earlier run dates the Assam copy 2025-01-31). Newer development missed: the earlier run's note on the CPCB categorisation page records a CPCB 'Classification of Waste Battery Collection Centre' dated 11 June 2026, which post-dates the 2025 list and bears on kabadiwalas and DWCCs taking batteries. Against the refined chain: the answer treats colour as a property of the business, but in the founder's model the consent-bearing step is a state transition (S3 baling is White; S4 shredding, S5 washing and S7 granulation are Orange or Red), so the rulebook should attach colour to the processing-record type, not only to the role.
verdicts.correction: Keep the counts and bands as dated rulebook data: 419 sectors (Red 125, Orange 137, Green 94, White 54, Blue 9), of which Annexure-I 'industrial sectors' is 359 (107/120/81/51), per the CPCB report the founder holds; PI Red >=80, Orange 55 to <80, Green 25 to <55, White <25; label the 60-sector remainder (9 Blue + 51 others) as 'derived by subtraction, not read from the report'. Store the Blue list and the +2-year CTO rule as 'reported by state boards and law-firm notes, list of nine not re-read', and keep both 'e-waste collection' and 'sewage/drainage networks' as disputed entries until Annexure III of the report is read. Do NOT hard-code Karnataka validity: record two candidate regimes - 5/10/15 years (claimed KSPCB notification of 3 June 2019, unverified) and 5/5/10 years (Notification 1425 of 15 June 2016, per the founder's sheet and the repo legal cluster) - and read validity off each unit's XGN consent order, which is the check the admin does anyway. Treat circular KSPCB/258/2025-SEE-1 of 28 March 2025 (effective 30 March 2025) as possibly Karnataka's adoption of the 2025 list, to be confirmed by opening the TeamLease note or asking KSPCB; until then 'KSPCB adoption date' is an open item. White exemption: G.S.R. 702(E)/703(E) of 12 November 2024 (39 industries, self-declaration) is well-attested; the 28 July 2025 widening to every PI<=25 sector is unconfirmed and should be marked so. Add the CPCB 'Classification of Waste Battery Collection Centre' of 11 June 2026 to the rulebook and read it before any battery listing. Model change: attach the consent colour to the processing step (state transition S3->S4, S4->S5, S6->S7) in each processing record, with the business's own consent order as the evidence, rather than to the role alone. Status stays 'partly'; who to ask is unchanged (KSPCB head office / Bengaluru regional office, an XGN-filing consultant).

verdicts.question: Under the 2025 classification and G.S.R. 702(E) of 12 November 2024, which of Luma.Green's roles need which consent: kabadiwala shop, baling yard, dry-waste centre or MRF, PET flake line, plastic granulator, cable granulator, tyre shredder, C&D crusher, e-waste dismantler, battery breaker, used-oil re-refiner, compounder? For each, the category, consent or authorisation, issuing body, what the public register shows, and the fee band.
verdicts.problems: Same verification limit: no fresh snippet could be obtained today (search budget exhausted, fetches refused), so checks rest on repository evidence. What holds: the core role-to-colour map is corroborated by an earlier run that opened the CPCB 2025 report and the KSPCB categorisation page - 'collection centres (without depollution, dismantling and shredding)' and 'bailing (hydraulic press) of waste papers' White, plastic flakes/granules Orange, aluminium/copper extraction from scrap Orange, lead-acid battery recycling Red, e-waste dismantling listed separately - and the XGN public register (opened 2026-09-29) shows unit, colour, order number and validity. Problems: (1) the fee band is presented as 'confirmed from the official page' (above Rs 1,000 crore: Red 2,00,000 / Orange 1,75,000 / Green 1,50,000 per year) while the same source entry says the KSPCB Consent Fee page was 'not opened'; no snippet with these figures exists anywhere in the repo, so the top slab is unconfirmed and the floor (Rs 200/150/100) comes from a 2009 article that is 17 years old - the whole fee band is an open item, not a partly-confirmed figure; (2) the 2023 'zonal SEO may accept a shorter fee period' note (TeamLease 29931) is not confirmed by snippet; (3) tyre colour is inconsistent across the repo: this answer says 'Red under the old KSPCB code 1424', the pre-processors cluster says 'Tyres (Orange 1424)', the founder's chain CSV says 'pyrolysis (Red 1178/1424)' - the answer should say the old-code colour is itself disputed; (4) 'e-waste cable granulator = Red (mechanical processing only)' under the 2025 list is not confirmed by snippet, only by the 2016-era Red listing; (5) the PWP register claim ('CPCB EPR-plastic portal lists registered PWPs') is stale against the sibling new-roles cluster, which records the standalone eprplastic portal being switched off on 28 June 2026 and data moved to the centralised EPR portal; (6) the 'kabadiwala ... from 1 April 2026 local-body registration under SWM Rules 2026 rule 9' date is not confirmed by snippet (the rules are S.O. 388(E) of 28 Jan 2026; the commencement date for rule 9 was not seen). Newer development missed: CPCB's 'Classification of Waste Battery Collection Centre' dated 11 June 2026 (noted on the CPCB categorisation page by the earlier run), which decides whether a kabadiwala or DWCC that accepts lead-acid or lithium batteries is a consent-exempt collection point or a registrable entity - directly relevant to the pilot's battery listings. Against the refined chain: the map is by role, but the founder's model makes every processing record produce a main output, by-products and residual waste as separate lots; the residual lots of Orange lines (PET wash sludge, plastic fines, cable insulation fluff, tyre fibre) and of Red lines (battery paste, e-waste residues) are hazardous or other waste that needs an authorised handler/TSDF and, for the generator, HOWM authorisation and Form 10 manifests - the answer covers HOWM only for battery and used-oil units. The compounder (S7->S8) and the 'intermediate processor' are treated as one; the answer's 'likely Green' for virgin compounding is a guess and should be an open item.
verdicts.correction: Keep the role map with these edits. Kabadiwala and paper/plastic baling yard (S1-S3): White or unlisted; no KSPCB consent, written self-declaration under G.S.R. 702(E)/703(E), GBA trade licence, local-body registration under SWM Rules 2026 (commencement date for rule 9 to confirm); if they take batteries, apply CPCB's 11 June 2026 'Classification of Waste Battery Collection Centre' (to be read) before allowing the listing. DWCC/MRF: Blue only at 5 TPD or more; below that the colour is an open item (default self-declaration, ask KSPCB); city agreement plus SWM 2026 registration either way. PET flake/wash line, plastic granulator, compounder using recycled feed (S4-S8): Orange CTE/CTO from KSPCB plus Plastic Waste Processor registration on the centralised CPCB EPR portal (the standalone eprplastic portal was retired on 28 June 2026 per the sibling cluster); compounder on virgin feed: colour open. Cable granulator: Red with E-Waste Rules 2022 registration if the cable is e-waste; plain scrap-cable granulation colour open (old list: copper recovery Orange); non-ferrous EPR registration from 1 April 2026 once the portal is live. Tyre shredder/crumb and pyrolysis: colour open (sources disagree Red/Orange; continuous pyrolysis reported Orange since the 23 Oct 2023 CPCB committee), waste-tyre EPR portal registration mandatory. C&D crusher: Blue, plus registration on cdwm.cpcb.gov.in. E-waste dismantler: Red plus eprewaste registration. Battery breaker: Red plus HOWM authorisation and eprbattery registration. Used-oil re-refiner: HOWM authorisation and eprusedoil registration; colour open (historically Red). Fee band: drop the 'confirmed' wording - the KSPCB consent fee is by capital-investment slab and paid upfront for the validity period, but no slab value is confirmed; read the slabs off the KSPCB Consent Fee page or ask the regional office; White is free; Blue at its PI colour is assumed for Karnataka. Public register: XGN 'All Consent Orders' (behind a CAPTCHA) for colour, order number and validity; the CPCB centralised EPR portal and the stream portals for registrations; BSWML's list for DWCCs. Model change: for every Orange and Red processing record, the residual-waste lot must carry a disposal route to an authorised handler/TSDF with the generator's HOWM authorisation and manifest number as fields, since the founder's model makes residues their own lots; store the consent colour on the processing-step type (S3->S4 shred, S4->S5 wash, S6->S7 granulate, S7->S8 compound) as well as on the business. Status: partly; the 11 June 2026 battery-collection classification and the fee slabs are the two items to close first.
